did_you_know.text: Did you know? Amaziah followed the principle that children should not be put to death for their fathers’ sins, but that each person should be punished for his own sin.
Did you know? Amaziah defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt, struck down ten thousand men, captured Sela, and renamed it Joktheel.

Did you know? Jehoash king of Israel responded to Amaziah with a parable: the thistle asked the cedar to give his daughter to its son in marriage, but a wild animal trampled the thistle. This parable warned Amaziah not to become arrogant over his victory over Edom.
Did you know? After Judah’s defeat at Beth Shemesh, Jehoash broke through Jerusalem’s wall for a distance of four hundred cubits, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.
Did you know? Jehoash took the gold, silver, and articles from the Temple and from the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
Did you know? After Amaziah’s death, the people of Judah made Azariah king, even though he was only sixteen years old.
Did you know? Azariah built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king’s death.
Did you know? Jeroboam son of Jehoash reigned over Israel for forty-one years, but Scripture notes that he continued in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Did you know? Jeroboam son of Jehoash restored Israel’s borders from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, just as the prophet Jonah son of Amittai from Gath-hepher had prophesied.
Did you know? Despite Israel’s sins, Scripture says that the Lord saw Israel’s deep suffering and bitter distress, and saved them through Jeroboam son of Jehoash.
